method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Medicare Levy Act 1986, Compilation No. 53, compilation date 1 July 2026, includes amendments up to Act No. 58, 2026 (Register id C2026C00295), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03351.txt (figures for 2025-26 and later); with dated arms from Compilation No. 50 (C2024C00076, in force 6 March 2024 to 31 December 2024; figures for 2023-24) at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03351.2024-03-06.txt and Compilation No. 52 (C2025C00323, in force 28 March 2025 to 30 June 2026; figures for 2024-25) at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03351.2025-03-28.txt, both retrieved 2026-10-21; with the formulas the text lost (ss 8(2), 8B(2)(b), 8C(3)(b), 8D(4)) transcribed by hand from the Word rendering of the same compilation in ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03351.formulas.md (2026-10-21); the low-income figures are in the Act's own text (no instrument sets them); which year each compilation's figures are for is an INFERENCE from the amendment history; Private Health Insurance Act 2007 ss 22-30, 22-35, 22-40, 22-45, 45-1 as deposited at ../../../private-health-insurance-act-2007/registers/source-bundle/C2007A00031.txt

scope: From the seat of the taxpayer: s 3(1) (threshold amount $28,011 or $44,268 with the s 160AAAA rebate; phase-in limit $35,013 or $55,335), s 3(3) (living apart; a spouse who died), s 3(5) with PHI Act s 45-1 (private patient hospital cover, excess $750/$1,500), s 3A with PHI Act s 22-30 (tier 1-3 earners; indexed tier thresholds and the s 22-40(4) child increase are inputs), s 6(1) (2%), s 7(1)-(2) (nil, then 10% shading-in), s 8 (family case; family income; family income threshold $47,238 + $4,338 per child, $61,623 for seniors, s 8(6) family tax benefit rule; the s 8(2) formula reduction (2% of the threshold less 0.08 x the excess, if any), from the formulas sidecar; s 8(3) apportionment; s 8(4) pass-over to spouse), ss 8B, 8C, 8D (surcharge 1%/1.25%/1.5% of taxable income for a whole year without cover, pro rata by days for part of the year; s 8D(3)(c) $28,011), s 9 (prescribed person part of the year). Dated arms: 2023-24 from Compilation No. 50 ($26,000/$32,500; seniors $41,089/$51,361; family $43,846 + $4,027, seniors $57,198), 2024-25 from No. 52 ($27,222/$34,027; $43,020/$53,775; $45,907 + $4,216, $59,886), 2025-26 and later from No. 53. Years before 2023-24 return 'Not in the deposited text'; a part-year surcharge with prescribed days or more than one section returns 'Not covered by this encoding'; s 9A lump sums in arrears return 'Not covered by this encoding'. Not encoded: s 6(2)-(6), s 7(3)-(4), ss 8E-8G, s 10 (trustees), s 9A, ss 1, 2, 4, 5, 11, rounding.
seat: the taxpayer (the individual on whose taxable income the Medicare levy and any surcharge are imposed)
